territory.label: The Receipt
territory.lens: itemized, audited transparency — every claim carries its number
territory.description: Treat the shoe like an invoice: publish the complete bill of materials, emissions and costs, and make checking the brand's work the core brand ritual.

big_idea: The Receipt Shoe: every pair ships with its itemized, third-party-audited footprint — 4.9 kg CO2e, 61% recycled-content upper, zero offsets purchased — printed on the tongue and living at a public URL that updates when the numbers do.

art_direction.imagery_direction: Forensic product macro photography under flat, even light: materials shot like lab evidence with their line-item data set beside them; no lifestyle gloss, nothing hidden in shadow.
art_direction.layout_notes: Invoice logic: strict column grid, tabular numerals, generous white margins; data rows set flush like a till receipt with a single accent rule.

copy.headline: Don't trust us. Read the tongue.
copy.subhead: Every pair publishes its audited footprint — materials, emissions, and the misses — where you can't avoid it.
copy.body: Most brands print a slogan on the tongue. We print the bill: 4.9 kg CO2e, 61% recycled upper, zero offsets, audited by people we can't fire. When a number improves, we update it. When it gets worse, we publish that too. You wouldn't train on vibes — don't buy on them either.

critique.case_against: The receipt mechanic lives or dies on the accuracy of its numbers: one methodology error or supplier misreport becomes a public correction that reads as the very greenwashing the brand attacks. Independent audits at seed-stage volumes are expensive and slow, per-SKU updates create real operational drag, and better-funded incumbents can copy carbon labeling faster than a startup can defend it. There is also a genuine risk the tongue-receipt reads as a gimmick after the first purchase, leaving little emotional residue to retain runners beyond the data itself.

annotations.text: Strongest opening position of the three — the receipt is demonstrable in five seconds at retail and impossible for incumbents to copy without exposing themselves. Before this goes anywhere near production: legal review on publishing audited numbers, and a plan for the first bad number.
